recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 6 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once, and BEFORE the implementation change it exists to judge was committed. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json or with any of the five earlier holdouts.
recorded.whyASIXTHHoldout: Holdouts 4 and 5 have both been read. Holdout 4 failed and was diagnosed; holdout 5 was frozen before the repair that followed, measured, and read in turn. The rule that produced each of them applies to them equally: once an independent holdout has been read, a fresh one is frozen before the next implementation change, or the following measurement is of a change tuned against the instrument meant to judge it. Both earlier sets are kept unedited with their results, and neither may be described as untouched independent evidence again.
recorded.whyEVERYSituationHereIsSL14OWNED: The property that made holdouts 4 and 5 answer the question, kept deliberately. Every scenario carries an SL-14 acceptance expectation - a blocked alias with a disposition owed, or the boundary assertion that nothing here may be offered recovery. `isSl14Owned` is true for all ten, so the closure rule's attribution exception is structurally unavailable and every breach here gates closure. A byte-identity audit of this set can buy it nothing.
recorded.whatWasKNOWNWhenThisWasAUTHORED: More than for any earlier holdout, and stated in full because the freeze is worth only what the disclosure is worth. Known: everything holdouts 4 and 5 measured, including the three causes of holdout 4's twenty failures in one hundred calls; that the boolean disposition and the derived capability bound were BOTH measured on the main set and REVERTED, the first for raising blocked-scenario failures from a 13-19 band to 30 per ten runs while not reducing discards, the second for redefining what six already-frozen scenarios measure; that the judge at this freeze builds a prompt byte-identical to 70f5f1e for all 71 scenarios in the six sets, proven mechanically; that the repair now proposed constrains the ANSWER'S SHAPE at the sampler - a strict JSON schema - wherever the Work list offers recovery, so an invalid `posture` becomes ungeneratable rather than discouraged; and that a single 25-call smoke run of the main set under it produced no discarded judgment and an 8.0% failure rate. NOT known: any behavior of it on any of the ten situations below, none of which existed before this file, nor on any holdout.
recorded.howDifficultyWasPLACED: The repair being judged removes ONE failure class - an answer whose shape the parser refuses - and helps with nothing else. So the difficulty here is deliberately concentrated where it cannot help: which path carries a responsibility once a retry is pointless, whether a recurrence is read as a recurrence, whether a gap becomes a recorded finding, whether an answered question stays answered, and whether a need that no longer exists is allowed to keep generating work. Eight of the ten carry blocked Work, as holdout 5 did, because authoring away from the situations the change touches would make the set worthless in the other direction.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove, and nothing more. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment - which path a responsibility takes once a retry is pointless - the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed. Narrowing it would score SL-4's ordinary judgment as an SL-14 failure.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by the selftest that audits every scenario file in this directory. Two conventions are followed here that the main set does not follow, and both are what the RUNTIME does: where a blocked item has already spent its one Supervisor retry the set declares `retryExhaustedAliases`, and where a blocked item needs a capability the Case no longer declares, the set declares `capabilityGoneAliases` AND leaves that capability off `availableCapabilities`. `supervise.ts` resolves both from durable state on every wake - the second from `required_capability`, the field `planRecovery` itself refuses on - so a situation where the capability is gone and the judge is NOT told is a state the running system cannot present. Holdout 4's two capability scenarios were authored before that wiring existed and asked the judge to infer the bound from failure prose instead; their result stands as measured and is recorded as a scenario-fidelity finding against that set, not reinterpreted.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. Nothing here moves one.
recorded.howThisSetMayBeUSED: Once. If its result is read and an implementation change follows, this set is observed too, and a further independent holdout must be frozen before that change.

bar_rationale: The five bars ratified for SL-14 / RS-2 on 2026-09-15, unchanged. This set is measured against them exactly as the main set is.

scenarios.label: A notary slot lookup blocked by a first technical failure, with the owner expecting the date
scenarios.rubric: The lookup failed once, the notary service simply did not answer, and the capability is still available. Retrying is the obvious recovery, and carrying the responsibility another way is also defensible. The failure says nothing about the prospect, and contact is unavailable, so nothing here may propose reaching them.

scenarios.label: The owner's answer settles what the blocked Work was trying to find out

The answer opens the next step.
